A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Polar Express work. Their text, equations, figures, algorithms, and complete appendices support reliable comparison across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v3 reports original matrix-convergence experiments, GPT-2 training results, and appendix experiments on initialization, runtime, and attention-head splitting.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds longer GPT-2 training, approximation-accuracy controls, singular-direction experiments, and image-classification results.

M1.justification: v4 corrects the offline Remez initialization: Implementation 2 uses (3*l+u)/4 and (l+3*u)/4 where v3 Appendix G used (3*l+1)/4 and (l+3)/4. The minimax composition, stabilization rules, cached coefficients, and online PyTorch implementation are otherwise retained.

E1.justification: Beyond v3's synthetic-matrix, GPT-2-gradient, and language-modeling evaluations, v4 adds CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 image classification (Appendix H.3). This substantially extends domain and task coverage. The FineWeb extension from 1B to 10B tokens changes training budget within retained coverage.

E2.justification: v4 adds exact-SVD Muon as an evaluated reference (Figure 5) and SGD with momentum to the image comparisons, which also include Muon with Newton-Schulz. Conversely, Chen–Chow's degree-3 comparator disappears from the Frobenius convergence comparison (v3 Figure 5; v4 Figure 8). Jordan and You remain the central language-model baselines.

E3.justification: v4 adds 10B-token training, 2–30-iteration and SVD controls, singular-value cutoff sweeps, cosine-similarity and projected-subspace evaluations, and vision training protocols. The Frobenius comparison changes one tested layer and Polar Express's lower-bound setting from 10^-4 to 10^-3. These extend and revise evaluation settings while retaining the original 1B-token GPT-2 protocol.

E4.justification: v4 adds substantial analyses connecting polar-approximation accuracy to optimization: iteration-count versus exact-SVD controls, zeroing or reversing small singular directions, and convergence restricted to dominant singular directions (Figure 5 and Appendix H.1). It also examines longer-training behavior. v3's initialization, stability, rectangular-matrix, and head-splitting analyses remain after relocation.

E5.justification: v4 Figure 3 identifies the previously unexplained convergence shading as a 90% interval over 512 data batches. Figures 14–16 report ranges across three random seeds for image training. These add explicit uncertainty reporting without establishing increased repetition of retained experiments; GPT-2 training gains still lack run-to-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Substantial results are added: 10B-token GPT-2-Large losses are 2.913 for Polar Express, 2.919 for You, and 2.921 for Jordan (Figure 6). CIFAR-10 ViT accuracy is 0.860 for Polar Express versus 0.874 for Muon–Newton-Schulz (Figure 16). These are new-setting results. Figure 12a also corrects v3 Figure 7's inconsistent Polar Express loss caption from 3.588 to 3.344.

T1.justification: The main optimality and convergence theorems and proofs are retained. Appendix J corrects the rectangular-method derivation's base case from q_0(x)=x in v3 Appendix F to q_0(x)=1, matching Q_0=I. Appendix H.1 adds formal truncated-polar and singular-subspace definitions supporting its new analyses.

C1.justification: The abstract extends the claimed GPT-2 validation-loss advantage from 1B to 1–10B FineWeb tokens. Section 1.3 newly reports adoption into the NanoGPT speedrun. The central contributions concerning optimal polynomial composition, convergence, GPU efficiency, and finite-precision Muon use retain their meaning.

C2.justification: v4 introduces a substantive explanation for why five or six iterations suffice: small singular directions appear relatively uninformative, while important directions converge (Appendix H.1). It also states that the language-model advantage shrinks with longer training and that image classification shows no consistent Polar Express advantage. These materially develop the mechanism discussion and applicability boundaries beyond v3.

D1.justification: v4 adds vision architecture and hyperparameter descriptions, identifies the SVD implementation, supplies a reproducibility statement, and clarifies the retained rectangular-matrix experiment. Existing code links remain. Documentation also loses v3's explicit Tiny Shakespeare identification for the gradient test, while Figure 9's new 'bfloat32' label leaves that experiment's precision unclear.

R1.justification: v4 adds inexact-Muon references by Shulgin et al. and Refael et al., connecting them to its convergence bound, plus references supporting vision experiments and compute-optimal training. The Karpathy dataset reference is removed. Positioning relative to Chen–Chow, Zolo-pd, Lee et al., and Grishina et al. is largely retained.

P1.justification: v4 substantially condenses and reorganizes the narrative. Related work moves to Appendix B, code is consolidated in Appendix A, and detailed Remez and stability explanations move out of the main text. It adds a dedicated ablation section, a structured experimental appendix, a contents page, and a reproducibility statement.

P2.justification: v4 changes typography and theorem styling, removes v3 Figure 2a while retaining 2b as Figure 2, and separates compact main-text validation plots from fuller appendix panels. It adds accuracy/runtime, singular-direction, longer-training, and vision figures, relocates retained figures, and revises axes, legends, and captions.

improvement.justification: v3 demonstrates approximation quality and GPT-2 training gains but leaves their connection largely untested. v4's SVD, iteration-count, and singular-direction controls substantially strengthen that connection. Longer-training and negative vision results also clarify practical limits. These gains in empirical justification and interpretation outweigh the removed Chen–Chow comparison and remaining reporting ambiguities, although the small language-model gains still lack run-to-run uncertainty.
